  • The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.
  • Recent findings suggest that the fresh youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable manufacturer. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly rolled out Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

The Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

Recent findings suggest that that setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

It has been revealed that there’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

The bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

The Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is right now offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The company notes preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

It has been revealed that that price also comes with something increasingly important in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual company standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, quickly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

There’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

When it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

It’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real company standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

South Korea will use emergency alert system to warn about exam cheaters

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Thursday morning, millions of phones across South Korea will belt out a loud, buzzing alert normally intended to warn residents about earthquakes or other disasters.
  • In a recent development, officials initiative to send the notifications ahead of Suneung, the country’s notoriously gruelling, eight-hour-long college entrance exam, in an attempt to flush out any of the roughly 550,000 test-takers who may have smuggled in a banned smartphone.
  • The aggressive, last-minute measures come just days after a student in a national tax accountant exam admitted he used a miniature camera and a generative AI tool to achieve a near-perfect score.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Thursday morning, millions of phones across South Korea will belt out a loud, buzzing alert normally intended to warn residents about earthquakes or other disasters. This time, the alert is targeting a much different kind of public threat: sneaky standardized test cheaters.

In a recent development, officials initiative to send the notifications ahead of Suneung, the country’s notoriously gruelling, eight-hour-long college entrance exam, in an attempt to flush out any of the roughly 550,000 test-takers who may have smuggled in a banned smartphone. Proctors will also inspect all pairs of glasses for hidden cameras, and students wearing clothes with buttons will have to cover them with stickers.

The aggressive, last-minute measures come just days after a student in a national tax accountant exam admitted he used a miniature camera and a generative AI tool to achieve a near-perfect score. That surprise revelation sent educators and officials scrambling to come up with solutions to instill confidence in the upcoming test.

It has been revealed that korea’s measures come as educators around the world are struggling to keep up with a growing arsenal of AI-enabled tools that make cheating easier than ever. But while AI is the focus today, students have been tinkering with fresh tech and other creative ways to skirt the rules for as long as tests have carried weight.

The sudden rule changes in South Korea come days after a 34-year-old man named Han Won-seok posted a video on his lawyer’s YouTube channel admitting he used AI to cheat on the country’s national tax exam. According to the Associated Press, Han scored 397.5 out of 400 points on the first stage of the multiple-choice test, a suspicious result that made him the subject of several media interviews. Other test-takers saw those results and accused him of trickery.

Industry observers note that days after denying those allegations, Han reversed course. In the video, he admitted to using a miniature camera to photograph the exam questions, which were then fed to an AI tool. He then viewed the AI-generated answers on his smartphone. Now, Han says he is cooperating with investigators and is warning others against following his lead.

“I cheated on the tax accountant exam. I sincerely apologize for causing damage to a lot of people,” the student mentioned in the video, according to CNN. “If there is someone thinking of cheating like I did, I’m going to tell the investigators everything, so I hope you don’t think that you won’t get caught.”.

It has been revealed that in the days since the videos, officials have rushed to put in place newly introduced anti-cheating safeguards. South Korean Prime Minister Han Sung-sook reportedly held a meeting on Monday with the country’s top education officials, where they agreed to officially add smart glasses to the list of prohibited items in testing rooms. Some lawmakers had reportedly even called on officials to postpone the Suneung exam until they could come up with more rigorous anti-cheating safeguards, though the country’s Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin rapidly shot that idea down, arguing delays would cause “even a larger disruption.” And while Han never said he specifically used smart glasses to cheat, worries about that tech in particular aren’t hypothetical. Earlier this year, two other South Korean students taking an exam to assess English skills were also caught using camera-equipped glasses.

Concerns about AI-enabled cheating aren’t limited to South Korea either. Last week, England’s Office for Students, an independent higher education regulator, released a statement warning that AI tools are making it “close to impossible” to assess university classwork. In China, major tech companies disabled features on their AI apps during last year’s national college entrance exam (the gaokao), to keep students from using them to cheat. Educators in the United States and elsewhere are also increasingly requiring students to take exams in person and defend papers orally due to the pervasiveness of AI-generated submissions. Sales of Blue Books have soared as a result.

Recent findings suggest that while fancy AI tools and camera-equipped smart glasses may be new concerns, creative cheating isn’t. In fact, evidence of sneaky test-takers dates back centuries. One example is this replica of a linen vest from China’s Qing dynasty (1644–1911). The impressive garment has 62 essays, more than 40,000 characters in all, hidden inside. Students wearing the vest would sneak peeks during the country’s grueling imperial exams, which played an key role in determining government employment and social status. An even older Ming Dynasty (1368 to 1644) jacket was covered with some 50,000 characters from classical texts likely served a similar purpose.

Creative cheating has of course persisted into the modern era. In 2015, police in India’s Bihar state detained more than 1,000 people after relatives of test-takers were photographed scaling the walls of an exam center to pass cheat sheets to students through a window opening. A college student in the U.S. made headlines in 2011, after he was arrested for allegedly using fake IDs to stand in for at least six high school students during SAT exams. In China, a team of exam proctors equipped with  surveillance drones regularly seizes a variety of wearables and other devices students use to try and cheat. Among the seized items were a hidden camera placed inside a pen and glasses with cameras connected to a tiny receiver embedded in a coin.

One has to wonder if all that time and effort spent devising intricate cheating methods could have been used to study instead.

Weight Gain During Long-Term Antipsychotic Use

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Industry observers note that most antipsychotics cause some degree of weight gain.
  • My first antipsychotic was Zyprexa, which I first started taking in 2001.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Industry observers note that most antipsychotics cause some degree of weight gain. They are generally classified into three categories according to the degree of weight gain each causes. Weight gain caused by antipsychotics can be a deterrent to using them, or a motivation to go off antipsychotics prematurely. For someone like me who has been on antipsychotics for 26 years, I have experienced a lifetime of managing weight fluctuation, gaining a good deal of weight and then losing it a few times. Here is an account of my journey of weight gain and loss while taking antipsychotics and what I have gleaned from these experiences.

My first antipsychotic was Zyprexa, which I first started taking in 2001. I was not informed by my psychiatrist at that time that this drug causes weight gain, and I was on a higher dose. Accordingly, I had no idea I was taking the antipsychotic notorious for causing the most weight gain, and the psychiatrist never shared with me the fact that the medicine could be a factor in my weight gain.

Sources indicate that I was already so hard on myself for taking an antipsychotic in the first place, and the weight gain, which I blamed on myself, was another source of shame. I couldn’t understand why I was gaining weight when nothing had changed with how much I eat and how much I was exercising, so I felt like my life was out of control in multiple ways. It felt similar to having some sort of mental illness but not really understanding what I was up against or what I could do about it.

Sources indicate that it’s so easy to be hard on yourself about weight gain, and it’s also so incredibly hard to properly attribute your medicine for causing it. Because of stigma, we are taught that mental illness should be under our control, just like society tells us that weight gain is really always under our control as well. Taking an antipsychotic can tug at your self-esteem, and weight gain just intensifies any tendency for low self-esteem and self-blame.

Sources indicate that I was on Abilify and experienced almost no weight gain with it, so I was happy. However, I suddenly started having involuntary tongue movements with this drug after it had worked well for me for years, so I had no choice but to go back on Zyprexa, just a month or two before I started trying on wedding dresses after my engagement. As someone who was anorexic in college and still body dysmorphic, gaining a bunch of weight right before trying on wedding dresses, when most people try to be their thinnest, seemed so unfair. I took it as a sign that I would never be able to move on with my life.

I was thankful that my psychiatrist put me on a high dose of Metformin to help manage weight gain caused by Zyprexa. The Metformin felt to me like validation and acknowledgement that, yes, it’s not all my fault if I gain weight on this drug and that there are real, demonstrated ways that psychiatry acknowledges and helps us with this issue. Even with Metformin, I put on 15 pounds, but I successfully worked hard to lose it all before it was time for dress alterations. But it did feel like an unnecessary hurdle and annoying complication, a reminder that my illness is never over.

I’ve gained and lost so many pounds through antipsychotic use. The weight creeps in until one day I’m forced to address it, then I go through an organized effort to lose it. Growing up, I was a competitive athlete who thought weighing 140 pounds was a lot, but for most of my adult life on antipsychotics, weighing 140 is no longer achievable, or if so, unsustainable.

I’m convinced the reason I gained over 60 pounds while pregnant with my child was due to being on Zyprexa at the time. However, I did lose the weight through walking, calorie reduction, and nursing. With the help of Metformin, I did not get gestational diabetes. I’m now on Quetiapine, and it is supposed to be a moderate weight gainer, but I don’t think I have much of an easier time keeping weight off with this drug than with Zyprexa. However, since Quetiapine is perfect for avoiding a terrible side effect I get with every other drug, there is no way I will ever take any other drug again. This time, when weight loss was called for at age 47, I needed to go on a GLP to lose it.

According to recent reports, one thing I can say about this 26-year journey of weight gain and dieting since I've been on antipsychotics is that I am healthier for it and make healthier choices. Because I have less control over my metabolism, I have made other critical health choices that will pay off in the long run in multiple ways. Giving up gluten is a substantial deal for me, especially with thyroid diseases, as well as giving up almost all soda and alcohol. I’ve also been a vegetarian for 20 years, for a number of reasons in addition to health. Some of these choices started as ways I could mitigate weight gain caused by antipsychotics, but they turned out to have benefited me in other very real ways.

In a recent development, another huge shift for me is caring more about my health than fixating on the number on the scale. I’m no longer concerned with going back to 140—I’m more interested in longevity and keeping up with my 7-year-old son. Through my cycle of weight gain and loss, I’ve given up on the idea that success is a clothing size; it’s about my bloodwork all looking good, reducing inflammation, feeling energetic, and exercising regularly.

In a recent development, one of the toughest aspects of serious mental illness is the elusiveness. You can’t visualize it; there is no blood test, and you may get re-diagnosed by different doctors. Sometimes there is no clear answer on what to do at all. You can’t control what effects antipsychotics have on you, and sometimes discerning what is under your control and what is being dictated by the antipsychotic is difficult. Weight gain caused by antipsychotics can feel the same way, leaving you feeling powerless and frustrated.

Industry observers note that it’s hard and seems unfair that making the right and responsible choice for your mental health can have other health consequences. But staying on antipsychotics, even if they cause weight gain, has been critical for my full remission from schizophrenia for 15 years and for becoming a wife and mother. Unpredictable weight gain has also led me to make key health decisions for myself when it comes to food and drink that will benefit me for the rest of my life. I’ve also made other good health choices that I probably would not have made if I did not have a tendency to gain weight due to antipsychotics. I’ve also learned to lean on internal means of validation and self-esteem instead of superficial, external means.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

It has been revealed that both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The California Department of Motor Vehicles has temporarily banned autonomous rideshare operator Waymo from operating on freeways in the Golden State.

The ban went into effect on November 11, and was prompted by an “imminent hazard to public safety,” according to the California DMV. The automotive regulator mentioned two specific incidents in which Waymo vehicles disregarded construction zones and law enforcement, pushed the ban forward, CNN reports.

The California DMV said Waymo will remain banned until it “demonstrates to the Department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.” Specifically, the Alphabet-funded autonomous vehicle operator will have to prove that its vehicles can safely detect and respond to construction zones and emergency vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that the freeway restriction applies to revenue ride-share operations, as well as test vehicles. Waymo will continue to operate normally on surface streets in its California markets. Currently, Waymo operates in Los Angeles, San Diego, and the Bay Area.

It has been revealed that “Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state,” Waymo remarked in a statement to Road & Track. “In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

One of the incidents that allegedly spurred this ban was caught on video earlier this month. The video demonstrates California Highway Patrol patrol cars creating a traffic break on Interstate 280 near San Francisco while a Waymo vehicle attempts to pass through the rolling roadblock. California Highway Patrol officers rapidly cut in front of the Waymo, which appears to stop the Waymo from attempting to pass again.

This is not the first time Waymo has faced scrutiny related to its highway operations. The manufacturer filed a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration earlier this year over driving software that repeatedly entered freeway construction zones. Waymo also briefly paused highway operations in San Francisco and Los Angeles this May over similar construction zone issues, according to CNN.

In a recent development, general Motors is looking for a new captain to steer the manufacturer, according to a story published on November 17 in the Wall Street Journal. The company is reportedly preparing for a future without CEO Mary Barra, who has led the automotive giant through a myriad of tumultuous times since taking the helm in 2014.

Industry observers note that according to the WSJ report, GM is working with an executive search firm in an effort to identify potential outside candidates to succeed Barra. That noted, the tech giant has not publicly commented on when the executive could step aside.

See all results for used cars for sale near 92612.

Sources indicate that having led the organization for 12 years, Barra is GM’s second-longest-serving CEO (the longest was Alfred P. Sloan, who lasted in the role for 23 years starting in 1923). She is also the first woman to lead a global automaker, and her time at the top of GM is about twice as long as the average tenure of modern S&P 500 CEOs, according to the WSJ.

In a recent development, barra has reportedly been laying the groundwork for her exit for several months. Despite looking at outside contenders, GM has a long history of selecting its chief executives from within the manufacturer, a move it could repeat when Barra exits. According to the WSJ report, top candidates for the role include the company’s finance chief, Paul Jacobson; the company’s top product officer, Sterling Anderson; and Mark Reuss, who has spent 40 years at GM, during several of which he served as Barra’s No. 2.

Barra took over the firm as it was still regaining its footing following its 2009 bankruptcy and has created a leaner but more profitable General Motors. The automaker sells millions fewer vehicles each year than it did a decade ago, although, thanks to a focus on higher-margin vehicles (specifically trucks), the automaker is generating record levels of profits. While the search is on to find an eventual successor, Barra told Fortune magazine in September that “I still feel like I can contribute and continue to build the foundation.”.

Sources indicate that jack Fitzgerald’s love for cars stems from his as yet unshakable addiction to Formula 1. After a brief stint as a detailer for a local dealership group in college, he knew he needed a more permanent way to drive all the new cars he couldn’t afford and decided to pursue a career in auto writing. By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job at Car and Driver. His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks.
  • Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the newly introduced “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.
  • That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance challenges with some of the game’s weapons and tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the newly introduced “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance challenges with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s enhancement, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Sources indicate that another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Recent findings suggest that beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

In a recent development, this change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

#52214. Latest Update: U.S. Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years, a Major Public Health Setback

Latest Update: U.S. Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years, a Major Public Health Setback

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1352 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, a major public health achievement that was secured 26 years ago.
  • Sources indicate that the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s (WHO) regional office for the Americas, determined that measles has spread continuously in the U.S.
  • “Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” PAHO’s director, Jarbas Barbosa, MD, MPH, PhD, mentioned in a media briefing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, a major public health achievement that was secured 26 years ago.

Sources indicate that the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s (WHO) regional office for the Americas, determined that measles has spread continuously in the U.S. for more than 12 months. On November 17, PAHO confirmed the end of the country’s measles elimination status, which it has held since 2000.

“Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” PAHO’s director, Jarbas Barbosa, MD, MPH, PhD, mentioned in a media briefing. “It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period of time, putting families and communities at risk of a preventable illness, hospitalization, and death.”.

PAHO’s review examined measles spread starting January 20, 2025, when the first person became ill in a large West Texas outbreak, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

According to recent reports, CDC data show 5,412 confirmed measles cases this year as of November 12. That’s the highest annual total since 1991 and more than double the 2025 count of 2,289 cases.

It has been revealed that andi Shane, MD, chief of pediatric infectious diseases at Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta, called the U.S. losing measles elimination status “a public health alarm that we are not being effective and we’re not controlling measles as well.”.

The measles virus is highly contagious. It spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. People can catch it in a room up to two hours after an infected person has left, according to the CDC.

“There’s really been very little measles in the United States over the past 25 years until January 2025,” William Moss, MD, a professor of epidemiology at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, told Healthline.

Industry observers note that losing the status itself doesn’t change much about daily life for most Americans, Moss remarked. The concern is the measles outbreaks, hospitalizations and deaths behind the loss, he said.

He called the loss “a big red flag” after “enormous efforts over the past 26 years” to keep the status.

It has been revealed that A country loses its elimination status when there is “uninterrupted circulation of the same virus genotype and lineage for 12 months or more,” according to PAHO. Shane explained it this way: “For the past 12 months in the United States, we’ve had ongoing circulation of the measles virus and person-to-person transmission is occurring.”.

Recent findings suggest that canada lost its elimination status in November 2025, and the U.K. and five European countries lost theirs earlier in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. can regain the status. “Other countries have done that,” Moss said. Brazil, which lost its status in 2019, regained it in November 2024. Venezuela, which lost its status in 2018, regained it in 2023, according to PAHO.

Before the measles vaccine, measles infected an estimated 3 million to 4 million Americans each year, according to the CDC. Among reported cases, about 400 to 500 people died each year, 48,000 needed hospital care, and 1,000 developed encephalitis, or brain swelling.

Here’s a timeline of measles elimination in the U.S.:.

Moss said elimination efforts “really intensified” after a large outbreak from 1989 to 1992. Part of that push was “really promoting school entry vaccination checks,” he said.

“That was one of the key policy changes that I think allowed for measles elimination in the United States.”.

Every state and Washington, D.C., require children to be vaccinated against measles to attend school, though exemptions vary by state, according to the nonprofit health policy organization KFF.

Fewer kindergartners are getting the MMR vaccine, according to the CDC.

It has been revealed that kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% in the 2019–2020 school year to 92.4% in 2025–2026. About 280,000 kindergartners started the 2025–2026 school year without records showing they had completed the MMR series, the CDC reported.

Shane remarked “95 out of 100 people need to be protected against measles” for a community to get herd protection.

“So since we’ve been below that for many, many months, that is also contributing to the loss of our elimination status,” she mentioned.

It has been revealed that “It takes two things to have a measles outbreak,” Moss mentioned. A community needs low vaccine coverage, and someone with measles has to enter it and “start the chain of transmission,” he said.

About 96% of this year’s cases were among people who were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status, up from 93% in 2025, according to the CDC.

Moss mentioned many of those cases are adults.

Recent findings suggest that “This is particularly true in Pennsylvania, where about two-thirds of the cases are in adults,” he mentioned. Many never got vaccinated as kids and grew up while measles was rare, so they never built natural immunity, he said.

He noted that having so many unvaccinated adults puts pregnant people and adults with chronic conditions like lung disease at risk of serious illness. The U.S. has already seen “dozens of pregnant women actually getting infected during pregnancy,” he mentioned.Infected parents can also spread measles to young children and grandparents, Shane said. Shane traced much of the hesitancy to the pandemic. “With COVID there’s been an overall distrust in vaccines and vaccination that initially started with COVID but has now spread to other vaccines,” she said.

Moss pointed to the federal government. “We know what it takes to achieve and sustain elimination. We have the expertise. We have the resources,” he said.

Industry observers note that he cited staff cuts at the CDC and said messaging from Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and President Donald Trump has undermined vaccine confidence. He called federal messaging on vaccines “really mixed and weak.”.

Moss also criticized the President’s August 10 executive order calling for the MMR vaccine to be split into separate shots for each disease.

“There’s no justification for that, and those vaccines don’t even exist in the United States,” he said.

According to recent reports, measles may cause ear infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, encephalitis and, in some cases, death, according to the CDC. The disease may also weaken the immune system for weeks to a year after recovery, raising the risk of flu, COVID-19, or RSV, Shane said. “It’s not a benign childhood disease,” Moss said.

The best protection against measles is two doses of the MMR vaccine, which are about 97% effective, according to the CDC. Shane said, “There are not very many other things we do in life that give you such great protection.” People who missed doses can still catch up, she added. “If you just don’t know or can’t tell, there’s no harm — as long as you’re eligible — in getting another MMR vaccine.”.

Shane added that “parents really want to do the right thing for their children.”.

According to recent reports, “We know that the MMR vaccine — that’s the vaccine that provides protection against measles — is a safe vaccine. It’s a very effective vaccine,” Shane said.

It has been revealed that babies under 12 months are too young for the vaccine. “So they depend on the protection of the people around them,” Shane remarked.

The CDC recommends a first MMR dose at 12 to 15 months and a second at 4 to 6 years. Babies 6 to 11 months old who will travel internationally should get an early dose, and adults without proof of immunity should get at least one dose, according to the CDC.

Recent findings suggest that to stop the outbreaks, Moss mentioned the U.S. will need to “increase vaccine coverage, particularly in those communities that have had long-standing low vaccine rates.”.

Sources indicate that so far, the response has been “more reactive than proactive,” Moss stated. Public health teams scramble once an outbreak starts, he said, and he wants more outreach to at-risk communities before measles arrives.

“I am worried about the ability of the United States to regain measles elimination status in the current climate,” Moss said.

Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • In a recent development, according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

In a recent development, according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

The Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout notes more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

According to recent reports, fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The tech giant claims the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Sources indicate that when Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout said it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then noted in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

It has been revealed that the product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

According to recent reports, for comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a significant number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

But validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where newly introduced automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

September 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

And the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

Industry observers note that but by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all strategy to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

#52212. Tech Report: How to Not Lose Your Cool This Holiday Season

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (926 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: How to Not Lose Your Cool This Holiday Season

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Industry observers note that while the holidays can bring a great deal of joy, they can also trigger anger in a lot of people.
  • It has been revealed that anger is a powerful emotion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Industry observers note that while the holidays can bring a great deal of joy, they can also trigger anger in a lot of people. Think having to face difficult people during annual social gatherings, being stuck in traffic or stranded at an airport because of delays, or feeling underappreciated for all the effort you’ve put into a holiday that others may not have acknowledged.

It has been revealed that anger is a powerful emotion. Chronically angry people are more likely to suffer from heart disease, diabetes, and impaired immune functioning. They're also more likely to have unhappy marriages, be lonelier, and struggle at work.

Anger itself is not the problem. It's a normal and healthy emotion like any other. But when it goes unchecked, it can make us do and say things that cause irreparable damage or act in ways we deeply regret.

To help you keep your cool this holiday season, here are five anger-management techniques you can start using—today.

According to recent reports, look around your surrounding environment and try to find five things that are blue. Alternatively, you can seek out five things that begin with the letter A. Either approach helps shift your attention from the source of anger to a neutral stimulus. This brief break helps you de-escalate through cognitive shifting by allowing your emotions to cool down. The more time we spend ruminating and focusing on what’s upsetting us, the more hotheaded we can become. Distraction techniques like these interrupt that anger-rumination-explosion cycle, reducing activity in the amygdala and allowing our heart rates and blood pressure to come back to baseline.

Inhale all the way. Hold your breath for three to four seconds. Exhale all the way (try to make your exhale longer than your inhale). Hold your breath again at the bottom of that exhale for another three to four seconds. Repeat several times until you feel a reduction in distress. This breathwork technique and others like it help regulate the nervous system by increasing activity within the parasympathetic nervous system—the branch of the autonomic nervous system undergirding resting and digesting functions—and downshifting activity within the sympathetic (fight/flight) nervous system.

It has been revealed that when you feel yourself getting heated, try to imagine the anger you’re feeling as an object in your body. First, where is it? Then, what does it look like? Feel like? What’s its temperature and texture; its weight? Be as descriptive as you can. Then, take a deep breath in and, with that breath, imagine creating space around the object in your body. On the exhale, imagine breathing out its intensity—almost like you’re cooling off the object of anger in your body.

Industry observers note that many studies have found that mindfulness techniques such as this help to ease anger, in part by creating some distance between you and the anger itself, so that anger doesn’t take you on as great a roller coaster ride. Taking time to visualize and work with the emotion in the body also helps slow you down, so you don’t knee-jerked-ly blurt out something nasty or otherwise act impulsively in a way that may haunt you (and possibly ruin Thanksgiving dinner).

Recent findings suggest that if you feel yourself starting to get worked up—you're gritting your teeth, your face is flushed, your breathing is shallow, your fists are clenched—see if you can excuse yourself to splash some very cold water on your face or hold some ice cubes to your chest or your temples. If you’re in a part of the world where it’s cold during the holiday season, go take a walk outside in the icy air. Exposure to very cold temperatures helps to trigger the diving reflex, which promptly lowers heart rate and can essentially shock your body back into a less elevated state.

It has been revealed that this one is especially helpful for dealing with difficult people over the holidays. If you’re surrounded by folks who aren’t aligned with you politically, can be quite rude, or make unnecessary comments about your life, body, or any other personal aspect, imagine a force field around you. Really go deep with the visualization here. What color is the force field? What is it made of—ice? Fire? Laser beams? Does it make a noise? Then, imagine the difficult person’s (or persons’) statements bouncing off of the force field (better yet, if they make a funny noise when they do so), leaving you safe and protected. You can go the extra mile and imagine the statements bouncing back and tripping the other person, spilling all over them, or whatever other amusing visual will bring you more of a smile than a grimace.

All of these techniques can be useful in moments of high frustration leading to intense anger. (I use them with my clients, and also with myself.) If you find yourself becoming angry quite often or if you find it particularly challenging to de-escalate and not do things you later feel badly about, it may be worth connecting with a therapist who can help you practice skills like these as well as do some deeper work around the origins of any chronic anger you may be struggling with. Don’t hesitate to get help if this is the case. Your heart health will thank you if you do.

We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn more ›.

Industry observers note that if you’re into personal audio, you might not want to spend all your money during Black Friday/Cyber Monday (but feel free to spend a little, and keep coming back here for some great suggestions as to how). Just within the last week, several innovative latest headphones and earbuds have been announced, so read on for wired, wireless, and TWS options for every taste.

It has been revealed that first up is Klipsch, the Hope, Arkansas-based heritage brand celebrating its 80th anniversary. But that doesn’t mean the acoustic design team is stuck in the past. Originally teased as Atlas at CES 2026 during a behind-closed-doors preview alongside powered standmount speakers and other surprises, the new Stratos Series uses an atypical (for headphones) two-way coaxial array, which aligns a mid/bass driver with a dynamic tweeter on a single axis to deliver low-distortion, high-efficiency, full-range sound.

The 380g Klipsch HP-2 (above) is the closed-back option, with a 40mm bio-cellulose woofer and 10mm tweeter achieving a frequency response of 15 Hz-18 kHz (+/-5 dB), plus isolation for more critical monitoring. The 458g HP-3 (below, and the one we’re most excited to audition) is a semi-open-back design that expands the woofer to 50mm to make up for some of the low end typically traded for a more expansive soundstage, and it achieves 16 Hz-22 kHz (+/-5 dB). Both promise “warm, punchy bass and crisp, sparkly highs,” and the pre-production units I heard in January delivered a good bright/bouncy balance, with rich, fun-colored but still composed mids as I recall (though it’s been many months removed).

Both models have an appropriately mid-century modern aesthetic, with auburn-stained sapele wood earcups and copper accents, machined aluminum yokes and contact points, Klipsch Heritage Twitchell grille cloth, replaceable microseude earpads, and protein-leather-wrapped open-cell-foam-filled headbands. Both 4.4mm balanced and 3.5mm unbalanced cables (plus a 1/4-inch adapter) with dual-mono connectors are included.

While both the Stratos HP-2 and HP-3 can be paired with smartphones and dongles of all sorts, they’ll really open up with a more refined signal chain, like the simultaneously announced $649.99 Onkyo HA-70, featuring two premium ESS ES9039Q2M SABRE DACs feeding an amplifier with plentiful inputs and three gain settings versatile enough to drive sensitive IEMs to 600Ω flagship headphones.

Compared to Klipsch, Brooklyn’s Grado Labs is a relatively young’un at the spry age of 73. First (and still) known for decades of producing phono cartridges, the family-owned manufacturer expanded into distinctive, hand-built headphones in the late ’80s (and still produces some fabulous flagships). The GW200 carries that tradition into something you can carry. The 235g GW200 takes a 44m S paper-composite diaphragm derived from the drivers in the company’s multi-thousand-dollar Signature line and puts it in an open-back wireless headphone. This helps deliver expressive bass and treble articulation within a frequency response of 16Hz – 34kHz.

Being open-back means a more spacious presentation with more instrument separation than your typical Bluetooth headphone (at the expense of isolation, of course, so don’t expect these to stand in for ANC travel headphones). Helping ensure this is Bluetooth 5.4 with support for Qualcomm aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC, plus 60+ hours of battery life. And there’s a single-sided 3.5mm audio input for passive use in case the battery does run out (or you just prefer an external DAC/amp combo).

Sources indicate that as for comfort and tuning, the GW200 comes with the Grado Labs F Cushions but is compatible with Grado’s complete line, so you can change both the physical and sonic feel by swapping them. Another trickle-down from the Signature series is the padded leather headband, which goes nicely with the matte black finish. We’re looking forward to getting a pair to try out.

Recent findings suggest that over in eastern Texas, Noble Audio has been producing artisan IEMs since the early 2010s (and founder John Moulton was doing custom in-ear monitors for enthusiasts even before that). In recent years, the organization has been showing what’s possible when the multiple-driver mentality of IEMs (some costing many thousands of dollars) is turned to portable audio, and the Astrid is the latest example. A tribrid architecture featuring an 8.3mm dynamic driver with a PU diaphragm and an aluminum-magnesium alloy dome, a 6mm planar driver, and one balanced armature in each earpiece, the Astrid brings a wired configuration and sophistication to true wireless earbuds.

It has been revealed that the overall tonality of the Astrid is rich, full-bodied, but not boomy … punch but not paunch. While sitting beneath the firm’s top TWS model, the 4-driver Prestige Encore, Astrid still delivers a detailed soundstage. What really brings the best out of it is the Audiodo Personal Sound feature, which uses a short tone recognition test to test each ear and saves per-channel adjustments on the earbuds to make up for any anatomically incurred frequency range deficiencies. Then Audiodo Equalizer lets you address sensitivities/preferences, overlaying further adjustments on your personalized curve (3-band on iOS, 5-band on Android). There’s also an assessment-independent 10-band EQ if that level of control is more your vibe.

In a recent development, to ensure the most cohesive playback possible, there’s multipoint Bluetooth 6.0 with high-resolution LDAC/aptX Adaptive support for compatible devices, as well as AAC and SBC. Plus active noise cancellation. Battery life is rated up to 11 hours on a single charge, with the wireless/USB-C case bringing the total carry capacity to 40 hours. All that is wrapped in IPX4 ABS enclosures featuring “divinely beautiful” glass fiber faceplates adorned with a dense lattice of silver filigree, like electro-acoustic etching … a metallic polyphony of colliding chords and intersecting transients.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ford may be talking up the fresh Fathom EV as its latest “Model T moment,” but the Blue Oval arguably already had one this century, and it’s called the Maverick. The compact unibody pickup landed in 2021 with a splash worthy of Homer Simpson off a high dive, thanks to its mix of truck bed utility, car-like ride and handling, and available hybrid power, all—technically if not practically—available for under $20,000.

Prices have admittedly climbed since then, even outpacing inflation, and the lineup has seen its fair share of rejiggering over the last five years; the standard engine switched from the hybrid setup to the turbocharged inline-four and then back to the hybrid, for example. The biggest change, however, has been the addition of more fun variants: the off-road focused Tremor and the on-road oriented Lobo, the latter of which aims to Ouija-board the spirit of the original F-150 Lightning to the best of its front-wheel drive-based capabilities.

But what if you already have a Maverick and want to add some zip? Or the Lobo’s just isn’t potent enough for you? Well, that’s where the latest Maverick SV300T Package comes into play. But you’ll have to pony up Mustang-like money if you want to see your new compact pickup come equipped with it when you pick up your zero-mile new rig at the local Blue Oval dealer.

Industry observers note that the package—which, regrettably, shoves the numerical portion of its name between the letters to keep it from being a proper SVT—comes from the Ford Custom Garage, Dearborn’s in-house upgrade division, and ties together official Ford Racing parts and other Ford accessories to make a sportier Maverick. It’s made for AWD XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models, with the marquee attracting an engine reflash and a Mustang EcoBoost-sourced turbo and an upgraded intercooler to push power from 250 hp and 280 lb-ft to 300 hp and 250 lb-ft; there’s also a Borla exhaust. XLT and Lariat rigs gain Maverick Lobo shocks, lowering springs, and upgraded stabilizer components; they can also opt for an available front brake upgrade. (When we tested it earlier this year on a short autocross course, we found the effects of both power and exhaust both quite noticeable, while the upgraded suspension amped up the delights in the turns.).

On top of that, Ford throws in a few visual upgrades to help make the SV300T’s presence known even before people hear that Borla exhaust. 20-inch wheels come in either black or bronze, as do matching hood and body graphics. Specific lettering on the tailgate also comes along for the ride, and XLT and Lariat trim versions pick up a latest lower front spoiler. Plus, if you buy the package with a new Maverick, performance-oriented tires are included, whereas customers adding it after purchase will have to pick them out separately.

Choosing to get the SV300T at purchase, however, means adding $13,395 to the price of a latest Lobo, and $15,595 to an XLT or Lariat. Granted, that includes installation and allows owners to wrap it into the truck’s financing, but that still pushes the price to $49,680 for the XLT and $48,090 for the Lobo, based on 2027 model year pricing. (Ford’s announcement claims it’s meant for 2025 and 2026 model year trucks, but considering it also mentions that the package is available on new Mavericks, it seems highly unlikely that it would not be available for 2027 ones too.).

It has been revealed that buy SV300T à la carte instead, and the pricing seems a bit more stomach-able; the XLT kit will run you $6075, and the Lobo version $4500. Keep in mind, though, doing so means you’ll have to have an ASE-certified tech handle the install, and you’ll still need to go out and buy new rubber on top of that to make the most of it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.
  • The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam.
  • The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

It has been revealed that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

Sources indicate that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

We at Car and Driver pride ourselves on our institutional knowledge and in-depth testing. It's why we've spent the last 70 years analyzing, reviewing, and testing the latest vehicles on the market.

If you want to know the ins and outs of just about any car sold in the United States, then you come to Car and Driver. And now, if you want to buy a newly introduced or used vehicle, then you . . . come to Car and Driver.

Recent findings suggest that specifically, the Car and Driver Marketplace. Powered by Autotrader, which offers one of the largest inventories of vehicle listings on the web, C/D Marketplace makes us a one-stop shop for researching and purchasing a vehicle.

In a recent development, not sure where to find or how to use our Marketplace? Then we've got you covered. Read on to see how easy it is to find your next car using C/D Marketplace.

Car and Driver Marketplace is for all shoppers in the market for a fresh or used vehicle—enthusiast and non-enthusiast alike. Whether you’re looking for a sports car to scratch your driving itch, a minivan or SUV for hauling the family around, or a pickup truck to take to work, you can use Car and Driver Marketplace to search through thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings.

Car and Driver Marketplace is a vehicle shopping tool for consumers in the market for a upcoming or used vehicle. We have thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings for vehicles being sold across the nation.

Whether you’re daydreaming about a certain make or model of vehicle, in the early stages of researching your next vehicle, or ready to reach out to sellers to purchase a new vehicle, you’ll find there’s no wrong time to use Car and Driver Marketplace.

Recent findings suggest that powered by Autotrader, Car and Driver Marketplace hosts one of the web’s largest inventories of newly introduced- and used-vehicle listings. But Car and Driver Marketplace doesn’t just help you find a new or used vehicle; it also helps you purchase one. With the ability to message sellers directly, submit offers, and calculate lease and finance payments, Car and Driver Marketplace can support just about the entirety of your car-buying journey from start to finish.

According to recent reports, enter the C/D Marketplace in one of two ways: from our home page or by going to caranddriver.com/cars-for-sale (feel free to bookmark it too).If you opt to enter C/D Marketplace from our home page, click on "Shop for Cars" on the top left of the page. Using a mobile device? Tap the drop-down menu on the top left of the page, then press "Shop for Cars" at the top of the list.

Once on the C/D Marketplace page, we recommend adjusting the filters. They appear on the left side of the page on desktop, and as a dropdown menu on the top left of the page on mobile.

Don't let the sheer number of filter options intimidate you. You can mess with as many or as few of them as you like. We do recommend at least filling out the "Location" field with your ZIP code and adjusting the radius of your search, which you can set from as few as 50 miles to the entire United States.

Some filters might be more crucial to you than others, such as the one labeled "Price & Payments" that allows you to set a price range for your search.

That's easy to figure out if you're a cash buyer, but what if you're looking to finance or lease your next car? Then click on the "Set Budget" link (or "Revision Budget" if you want to make adjustments to your already set budget). Toggle "Show Payments on Listings" too.

Recent findings suggest that after you click the "Set Budget" (or "Upgrade Budget") link, a pop-up window appears. It allows you to input your budget, the trade-in value of your vehicle (assuming you have a trade), and the amount you're planning to spend toward the down payment.

In a recent development, once you enter this information, you have the option to further granulate your monthly payment plans for the car you're interested in. You can set your budget for either leasing or financing. (Click the "Return to Dashboard" link after making an individual adjustment to get back to the pop-up window's home page.).

Industry observers note that now, go to the upper right side of the screen and click on the "Sort By" drop-down menu to make sure C/D Marketplace is presenting listings in your preferred order. Mobile owners will find this setting under the "Filters" menu at the top left of the screen.

The page defaults to sorting by relevance to your query, but you can also have it sort by price (lowest or highest), distance (closest), date (oldest or newest posted), vehicle mileage (lowest or highest), or model year (newest or oldest).

You're ready to scroll through listings now. See something you like? Click on it! Here's an example of what an individual listing page looks like. We picked a listing of our EV of the Year–winning 2025 Porsche Taycan in GTS form as an example.

As seen here, individual listings allow you to open up additional images of the vehicle, see basic specs (more detailed ones are available if you scroll farther down the page), adjust your spend, and even send a message or an offer to the seller.

Industry News: Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (885 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the firm to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the firm to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

In a recent development, the manufacturer started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

In a recent development, but then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

Industry observers note that the video indicates two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving quickly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation says that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the organization to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

According to recent reports, the DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It remarked that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

In a recent development, this is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

While the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Revision: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

Breaking: Rare rhino birth caught on camera at England’s Chester Zoo

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England.
  • The sex and weight have not been declared yet, and the calf also does not have a name.
  • At birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England. Even more exciting, CCTV cameras captured the poignant moment for this threatened species. The footage demonstrates rhino mom Asha giving birth, and the calf’s first unsure steps into the world.

The sex and weight have not been declared yet, and the calf also does not have a name.

At birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds. By comparison, the largest adult greater one-horned rhinos weigh over two tons, or as much as a car.

Industry observers note that the team used a combination of experience and non-invasive testing to help plan out the pregnancy. They closely monitored Asha’s behavior and regularly collected samples of her poop. By testing hormone levels in the samples, they could track Asha’s reproductive cycle and identify when she would be most open to mating. This helped the team safely introduce her to Beni the rhino, while a separate analysis helped confirm the pregnancy.

Sources indicate that “Asha was pregnant for about 15 months, so it’s a long wait! We had our fingers crossed when she highlighted signs of labour and we knew we were likely to welcome the calf very soon,” Emma Evison, Team Manager for rhinos said in an e-mailed statement. “It was a big moment for us—and for the conservation breeding programme—when the calf arrived. Any birth can be risky, even for an experienced mum, but fortunately everything went smoothly. The calf was up and about within an hour and feeding shortly afterwards. Asha knows exactly what she’s doing.”.

In a recent development, both mother and calf are reportedly in good health. They remained inside for the first few days following the birth to stay warm, but are now venturing to a special behind-the-scenes paddock outside of the enclosure. The calf is Asha’s fourth with father Beni. Sadly, Beni died in September following a sudden and brief illness.

“Beni was a lovely rhino. He was calm and approachable, helped train animal care specialists and even took part in animal behaviour studies,” added Tom Garland, Assistant Manager of the rhino team at Chester Zoo. “It’s lovely to know that his legacy lives on through this calf.”.

Recent findings suggest that while not the largest rhino species in the world, greater one-horned rhinos stand about six feet tall at the shoulder and are the biggest in Asia. They have the smallest horns of any rhino, but also have the biggest teeth. The males will sometimes use these chompers to bite each other while sparring. Currently, about 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos are alive today. They live in India and Nepal, in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. In the early 1990s, trophy hunting and habitat loss almost drove them to extinction.. Poaching for their prized horns also threatened their survival.

While the IUCN Red List of Endangered Species currently lists them as Vulnerable, they remain  at risk of extinction. Many of the rhinos are concentrated into a relatively small number of protected areas, putting their genetic diversity at risk. A lack of genetic diversity can lead to inbreeding and worse health outcomes in general. This fresh calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding program to help maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos living in human care.

Recent findings suggest that “Supporting Asha’s pregnancy has been really exciting,” added conservation scientist John O’Hanlan. “She’s one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is crucial in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population.”.

Upcoming Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50
